Reading

The innocent reading first. Under the exact-match operator the Overview identifies the piece, gives both names of its byline, places it in Pearl and Other Poems as its footnote, and describes its operation as a parody of Kerouac that moves his rules for spontaneous writing into telepathy and mind control. It gives the two authors as figures of experimental literary projects, fictional personas and online literature discussions, and offers two next steps: Kerouac's thirty points, or the background of Lee Sharks and Jack Feist. Its sources are the archive's capture records, the IDP map of the book, a Medium post carrying the book's contents, and the 2014 forum posting of the text. The results page below adds the Hugging Face poetics dataset (pearl/12), an Academia.edu PDF of the book whose contents set the Footnote at page 19, four more of the archive's capture records, and the forum's search page with the thread's tags.

Findings
  • THE WORK HELD, UNDER KEROUAC'S FRAME. The referent is right: byline, book, place in the book, premise. The frame is the one the critical edition was written against: the piece is a parody of Kerouac. Kerouac supplies its frame and one of its voices; the Overview takes the frame for the whole (critical edition, §§6.1, 7.4).
  • THE COMPOSITION READS THE ARCHIVE'S RECORD OF ITS OWN EARLIER READINGS. Three of five source cards are archive-controlled, and two of those are records of machine compositions: a capture of 2026-10-05 and TL;DR:009 (#603), whose AI Mode table first paired 'Jack Kerouac (Original)' with 'Lee Sharks (Parody/Extension)'. The Kerouac frame recorded by the archive as a machine reading returns as the machine's description.
  • THE VENUE MADE THE GENRE. 'Collaborative online forum text' takes the Online Literature Network posting of 6 December 2014 (cited) for the kind of work: a witness of the text, posted by its author five days after the blog, becomes what the text is.
  • THE BOOK DESCRIBED BY ITS LATER APPARATUS. Pearl and Other Poems (2014) is an 'experimental poetry and metadata project': the book is described by the machine apparatus of 2026 that its sources carry (the IDP map, the MPAI post).
  • THE NEXT STEP IS KEROUAC. The first follow-up offered is 'Detail Jack Kerouac's original 30 points from his modern prose manifesto'. The unquoted address takes that step without being asked (btp-aio-20261028).
  • WITNESSES IN THE ORGANIC LAYER. The results page carries two witnesses the archive does not hold: the Online Literature Network thread 'BELIEF & TECHNIQUE FOR TELEPATHIC PROSE, Lee Sharks & Jack Feist', started by illiterati on 12-06-2014 at 12:28 PM, whose search listing shows the tags 'allen ginsberg, emily dickinson, ernest ...'; and an Academia.edu PDF of Pearl and Other Poems whose contents set the Footnote at page 19, against page 23 in the New Human Press book (#1121), a different state of the book. Both are wanted by the critical edition (§2).
Analysis analyst prose, not machine text

Quoted, the title resolves to the work, and the work arrives inside the frame the archive has spent the most effort recording as a machine error. The composition's sources explain why: it reads the archive's records of earlier compositions, so the earlier compositions' frame is the frame it finds. What it adds is its own: the forum posting becomes the genre, and the 2014 book becomes a metadata project. Its offered next step is Kerouac's list, and the unquoted address, seated the same day, shows that step taken by the Overview unasked. The organic layer under the panel holds better material than the panel composes from: the forum thread of December 2014 with its tags, and a second state of the book.
